questions.question: Which famous Rashtrakuta king built the rock-cut temple of Kailash at Ellora?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**__Krishna I__

__
 
• He conquered the territories that were still under the Chalukyas
 
• He also occupied Konkan.
 
• Krishna I also defeated Vishnuvardhana of Vengi and the Ganga king of Mysore.
 
• He was a great patron of art and architecture.
 
• The Kailash Temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.
 
• The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples and monasteries located along the sloping basalt cliff at Ellora Caves.
 
• Generally, most of the excavation was completed by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (r. c. 756 - 773) in the eighth century, although some elements were added later. 

 [IMAGE: https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/66499582.cms?resizemode=75&width=1200&height=900] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __Govinda III (793 - 814)__

__
 
• The Rashtrakuta king who defeated the Pratihara ruler Nagabhatta II was Govinda III
 
• Pala King Dharmapala and his protégé Charayudh sought the help of Govinda III.
 
• His kingdom spread up to the Vindhyas and Malava in the north and the river Tungabhadra to the south.
 
• Govind III's northern campaign was not for empire expansion but for fame.
 
• Govind III defeated Pratihara king Nagabhatta II in 793 - 814 AD.
 
• Govind III further defeated the Pallava king Dantivarman in 803 at Kanchi.

**Jai Chand:**

 
• King Jai Chand__ was defeated by **Muhammad Ghori **in the Battle of Chandawar.
 
• The **Battle of Chandwar** took place between **1193 and 1194 CE.**
 
• **Prithviraj Chauhan** was the king of **Chauhan dynasty**, reigns between **1178 to 1192 CE.**
 
• Bhima II was a member of the **Chaulukya or Solanki dynasty**, reigns between **1178 to 1240 CE**.
 
• Kumarpala was an Indian king from the Chaulukya or Solanki dynasty of Gujarat reigns between **1143 to 1172 CE.**

questions.question: Commercial banks keep their deposits with RBI. These deposits are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **reserves**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR): is a specified minimum fraction of the total deposits of customers, which commercial banks have to hold as reserves either in cash or as deposits with the central bank.
 
• CRR is set according to the guidelines of the central bank of a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• 
 
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):- RBI has mandated every bank to have specific proportions of deposits in the form of liquid assets, exclude CRR is called Statutory Liquidity Ratio.

 
 
• 
 
Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) Rate is the rate at which RBI lends funds overnight to scheduled banks, against government securities.

questions.question: Pandit Rajendra Gangani is associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Kathak dance**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Kathak dance

__
 
• ​One of the eight primary styles of Indian classical dance is kathak.
 
• It is an Uttar Pradesh classical dancing style.
 
• The storytellers or itinerant bards known as Kathakars in ancient northern India are often credited as the creators of Kathak.
 
• The Vedic Sanskrit words Katha, which means "story," and Kathakar, which means "the one who tells a story" or "to do with stories," are the roots of the word Kathak.
 
• Traveling Kathakars used dance, songs, and music to transmit tales from the great epics and ancient mythology. 
 
• Kathak dancers use intricate footwork, flexible body movements, and, most importantly, expressive face expressions to convey a variety of stories.

 
• Pandit Rajendra Gangani is a renowned Kathak dancer trained in the Jaipur Gharāna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Odissi Dance:

 
• Odissi is a folk dance form of Odisha.

 
• This is a delicate dance backed by soothing lyrics and Is similar to Bharatnatyam in terms of Mudras and Expressions. 
 
• The cave of Udayagiri-Khandagiri provides the earliest example of Odissi.
 
• It was primarily practiced by Maharis under patrons of Jain King Kheravela.
 
• "Mobile Sculpture" includes two major postures: 
 
 
• Tribhanga - The body is deflected at the neck, torso, and knees.
 
• Chowk - A position imitating a square.
 
 
 
• Indrani Rehman, Charles Fabri, Guru Pankaj Charan Das, and Kelu Charan Mohapatra are some of the famous artists of Odissi dance.

questions.question: The popular style of temple architecture in northern India is called ________.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Nagara**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Northern India saw a rise in the popularity of temple architecture in the Nagara style.
 
• It typically lacks ornate boundary walls or entrances.
 
• The tallest tower is always exactly beneath the garbhagriha.
 
• There is an installation of Amalaka or Kalash on Shikhara.
 
• Nagara temples can be divided into many different types according to the shikhara's shape:
 
 
• Valabhi: Temples built in the Valabhi style are rectangular and have barrel-vaulted roofs.
 
• Wagon vaulted buildings and constructions get their name from having a vaulted chamber roof.
 
• Phamsana: These are shorter, but wider constructions made comprised of roofs with multiple slabs that rise up in a gradual slope on a straight incline like a pyramid meeting at one point over the middle of the building.
 
• Rekha-Prasad: A straightforward Shikara with a square base and inwardly curved walls with a pointed top distinguish Rekha-Prasad or Latina temples.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The Pallavas ruled over parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and northern Tamil Nadu until the ninth century.
 
• They are credited with developing the Dravidian style of temple architecture in South India.
 
• A compound wall encloses the Dravida temple.
 
• A Gopuram, or entrance doorway, is located in the middle of the front wall.
 
• The vimana, or main temple tower, is shaped like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The word "shikhara" is only used to refer to the crowning part at the top of South Indian temples.
 
• It is typically formed like a tiny stupika or an octagonal cupola.
 
• The garbhagriha's entrance is adorned with ferocious Dvarapalas, or the doorkeepers guarding the temple.
 
• A sizable water tank is frequently found encased within the complex.
 
• There are divisions among Dravida temples. These are basically five different shapes:
 
 
• square, kuta, and also caturasra.
 
• rectangular or shala or ayatasra.
 
• elliptical, coming from wagon vaulted shapes of apsidal chaityas with a horseshoe-shaped entry facade typically known as a nasi, also known as elephant-backed or vrittayata.
 
• circular or vritta.
 
• either ashtasra or octagonal.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Electric charge is a scalar quantity.
Electric charge is a vector quantity.

questions.solution:
Correct Answer **__Electric charge is a vector quantity__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Properties of electric charge 

__
 
• The electric charge on an object is not affected by the motion of that object, unlike mass. 
 
• **Electric charge **is additive in nature as the algebraic sum of charges located at various points on an object gives the** total charge on the object.**
 
• The** charge of a system **is always conserved that is, the charge **can neither be created nor destroyed.**
 
• The total charge on an object is said to be ***n e* **where **n** is an integer. Thus, showing charge is **quantized.**
 
• The** magnitude of both positive** and **negative charge** is **1.6 × 10-19 C.**
 
• Also, unlike charges attract each other, and like charges repel each other.

Explanation:__

**Electric charge** is invariant; it does not change with a **change in velocity.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The smallest unit of an element that has all the chemical properties of the element is called as an atom.
 
• Atoms are made of the three smallest particles- electrons, protons, and neutrons.
 
• The protons and neutrons remain in the nucleus of the atom and electrons revolve around the nucleus.
 
• The electrons are negatively charged, protons are positively charged and neutrons are neutral.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• The atoms of an element are neutral in nature because it contains an equal number of electrons and protons.
 
• If some of the free electrons are removed from the atom then the number of protons increases with respect to the number of electrons and the atom becomes positively charged.
 
• If some of the electrons are added to the atoms then the number of protons decreases with respect to the number of electrons and the atoms become negatively charged.
 
• The number of protons is always equal to atomic number of the atoms.

questions.question: In which year did the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II appoint the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1765.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

 
• In 1765 the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II appointed the Company as the Diwan of the provinces of Bengal.
 
• After the defeat at Plassey, Sirajuddaulah Nawab of Bengal was assassinated and installed the puppet Nawab of Bengal Mir Jafar.
 
• When the company interferes in the internal matter of administration Mir Jafar protested, the Company deposed him and installed Mir Qasim in his place.
 
• When Mir Qasim complained, he in turn was defeated in a battle fought at Buxar (1764), driven out of Bengal, and Mir Jafar was reinstalled.
 
• Nawab had to pay Rs 500,000 every month but the Company wanted more money to finance its wars, and meet the demands of trade and its other expenses.
 
• The Company wanted more territories and more revenue. By the time Mir Jafar died in 1765 the mood of the Company had changed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for slowing down of the Non-cooperation Movement?

options.text: Due to the absence of alternative Indian institution, boycott of British institutions posed a problem.
Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
Many lawyers resigned but then absence of income for a longer period of time compelled them to rejoin.
Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth and poor people could not afford to buy it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void. **

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**The Non-cooperation movement:

 
• It was launched on 5th September 1920 by the Indian National Congress (INC) under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• In September 1920, in a Congress session in Calcutta, the party introduced the Non-Cooperation program.
 
• Non-Cooperation Movement was a sequel to the Rowlatt Act, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, and the Khilafat Movement.
 
• It was approved by the INC at the Nagpur session in December 1920.
 
• Khadi & Charkha became a symbol of NCM.
 
• The main aim of the Non- Cooperation movement was:
 
 
• Work for the eradication of untouchability from society.
 
• Adopt Swadeshi habits including hand spinning and weaving.
 
• Adopt Swadeshi principles.
 
 
 
• The whole movement was abruptly called off on 11th February 1922 by Gandhi following the Chauri Chaura incident in the Gorakhpur district of UP (22 policemen burnt).
 
• Thus, we can conclude that the main reason for calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhiji in 1922 was that a police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh was set on fire by a mob.

questions.question: Amoeba acquires its food through the process of ______.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **endocytosis**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Amoebas** acquire their food through the process of **phagocytosis**, which involves extending their **pseudopodia (temporary protrusions of the cell membrane)** around a **food particle** and then engulfing it into their **cytoplasm. **
 
• Once inside the cell, the **food particle** is enclosed in a **food vacuole**, which then **fuses** with lysosomes for digestion.</str

questions.question: The part of the Himalayas lying between Satluj and Kali rivers is known as _______.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Kumaon Himalayas.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__Divisions of Himalayas: __The Himalayas have also been divided on the basis of regions from west to east.

These are Punjab Himalayas, Kumaon Himalaya, Nepal Himalayas, and Assam Himalaya.

__
 
• The divisions of the Himalayas that have been demarcated by the river valleys are:

 
 

 Nepal Himalayas
 The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Kali and Teesta is known as the Nepal Himalayas.
 
 

 Kumaon Himalayas
 The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Satluj and Kali is known as the Kumaon Himalayas.
 
 

 Assam Himalayas
 The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Teesta and Dihang is known as the Assam Himalayas.
 
 

 Punjab Himalayas.
 
 
The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Indus and Satluj is known as the Punjab Himalayas.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The main Himalayan river systems are those of the Indus and the **Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system.**
 
• The Indus, which is one of the great rivers of the world, rises near Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through India, and thereafter through Pakistan, and finally falls in the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
 
• The Brahmaputra marks the easternmost boundary of the Himalayas. Beyond the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas bend sharply to the south and spread along the eastern boundary of India.
 
• To the south of the main Himalayas lies the Pir Panjal Range at an average height of 5,000 meters (16,000 ft).
 
• From Gulmarg, in the northwest, it follows the southern rim of the Kashmir valley to the Banihal Pass.
 
• Here the Pir Panjal meets the ridgeline that separates the Kashmir valley from the Warvan Valley.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pair of micronutrients?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Calcium and fats**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__Concept:__

__
 
• Nutrients are the substances that are required by the organism/ plant to survive, grow, and reproduce.
 
• In the case of plants, different nutrients are absorbed by the roots and are then transported to the rest of the plant body.
 
• Xylem helps in the transportation of water, minerals, and nutrients in plants.

Explanation:__

An element is regarded as essential for a plant based on the following criteria:

 
• An element should be essential for the normal growth and reproduction of the plant.
 
• A requirement of an element should be such that it cannot be replaced by any other element.
 
• The element should be directly involved in the metabolism of the plant.

Based on the above-mentioned criteria and the quantitative requirements, nutrients are classified into two groups: Macronutrients and Micronutrients

Macronutrients:

 
• Macronutrients are needed in larger amounts by the plant tissues for their survival, growth, and other essential functions.
 
• Carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), potassium (K), calcium (Ca), and magnesium (Mg) are the macronutrients required by plants.

Micronutrients:

 
• Micronutrients are needed in smaller amounts by the plant tissues.
 
• Micronutrients required by plants are iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), copper (Cu), molybdenum (Mo), zinc (Zn), boron (B), chlorine (Cl), and nickel (Ni).
 
• Apart from these essential elements mentioned above, elements such as sodium (Na), silicon (Si), cobalt (Co), and selenium (Se) are also required by some higher plants.

questions.question: The largest dam in India, the Hirakud Dam, is built on which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Mahanadi__.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• Hirakud Dam is the longest earthen dam in the world.
 
• It is constructed across the great river Mahanadi.
 
• The bulk of the Hirakud dam contains earth, concrete, and masonry materials.
 
• From horizon to horizon the reservoir forms the largest artificial lake in Asia with an area of 746 sq. Km. and shoreline over 640 Km.
 
• The project was formally inaugurated by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on 13th January 1957.
 
• The installed capacity for power generation is 347.5 MW through its two powerhouses at Burla, at the right bank, and Chiplima, at 22 km downstream of Dam.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Godavari:**

 
• The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over the States of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry (Yanam).
 
• The other names for the Godavari River are The Vriddh (Old) Ganga or the Dakshin (South) Ganga.
 
• Godavari river drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Godavari river originates from Bramhagiri mountains at Trimbakeshwar.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner, and the Sabri.
 
• The longest tributary- The Manjira
 
• The largest tributary- The Pranhita

**Kaveri:**

 
• The Kaveri river is an Indian river flowing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and the Union Territory of Puducherry.
 
• The Kaveri river rises at Talakaveri on the Brahmagiri range (Karnataka) in the Western Ghats.
 
• It is the largest river in the state of Tamil Nadu and the third largest river after Godavari and Krishna in South India.
 
• Amaravati, Bhavani, and Kabini are the tributaries of river Kaveri.
 
• The Stanley reservoir on the Kaveri river in Tamilnadu is also known as the **Mettur dam.**

**Tapi:**

 
• The Tapti (also known as the Tapi) is the second-largest west flowing river in Peninsular India and is known as ‘the twin’ or ‘the handmaid’ of the Narmada.
 
• It flows for about 724 km before outfalling into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Cambay (Gulf of Khambhat).
 
• The Tapti River along with its tributaries flows over the plains of Vidharbha, Khandesh, and Gujarat and over large areas in the state of Maharashtra and a small area in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
 
• Situated in the Deccan plateau, the basin is bounded by the
 
 
• Satpura range on the north,
 
• Mahadev hills on the east,

questions.question: Which team has won the season 8 of Pro Kabbadi league?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Dabang Delhi K C.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Dabang Delhi KC clinched the Pro Kabaddi League Season 8 trophy by eking out a close 37-36 win over Patna Pirates __in the summit clash on 25 February 2022.

• The league's inception was influenced by the popularity of the Kabaddi tournament at the 2006 Asian Games.
 
• The format of the competition was influenced by the Indian Premier League.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Right to constitutional remedies.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Fundamental Rights (FRs) are known as the base of the Indian constitution & mentioned in Part III of the constitution.
 
• They prohibit unreasonable interference of the state & prevent its executive & legislature to become authoritarian, hence putting due limitations on state power.
 
• Observance of fundamental duties is required for having one’s FRs redressed in case of their violation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points:__**

__
 
• FRs are not absolute but qualified rights.
 
• It is Subject to certain restrictions imposed by the state on the question of national security, interest & general welfare of the society.
 
• But restrictions are checked by SC & HCs, whether restrictions are reasonable or not.
 
• SC verdict in the Golaknath V/S state of Punjab (1967) - FRs have been given a transcendental position by the constitution hence no authority functioning under the constitution including parliament has the power to amend FRs.
 
• In Keshavananda Bharati V/S state of Kerala, 1973, SC held that parliament has the power to amend any provision of the constitution including part III, however, parliament’s amending power subjects to the “Basic structure of the constitution".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

There are six Fundamental Rights-

 
 

 Article 14 – 18
 Right to Equality
 
 

 Article 19-22
 Right to Freedom
 
 

 Article 23-24
 Right against Exploitation
 
 

 Article 25-28
 Right to Freedom of Religion
 
 

 Article 29-30
 Cultural & Education Rights
 
 

 Article 32
 Right to Constitutional Remedies

questions.question: Which of the following states has one house in its state legislature?

__
 
• A legislature with two houses, or chambers. 
 
• The British parliament is a bicameral legislature, made up of the House of Commons and the House of Lords.
 
• A bicameral system is a reference to a government with two legislative houses or chambers.
 
• Bicameral is the Latin word that describes a two-house legislative system.
 
• The bicameral system originated in England, and the U.S. adopted that system upon its founding. 
 
• A bicameral system is a government style with two separate divisions within the legislative branch of government, versus a unicameral system that does not divide the government branch.
 
• A state legislature that has one house, known as Vidhan Sabha or Legislative assembly, is a unicameral legislature.
 
• In India, the two houses of the state legislature are – Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.
 
• There are only six states which have two-tier legislatures – Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana.
